page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized eighth-generation instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton processors with Neoverse-V2 cores. The instance features 8 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. It is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-dense 2 GB per core ratio. Cache layout includes 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. Local ephemerally attached storage is provided via a 474 GB NVMe SSD, managed through the AWS Nitro hypervisor alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the c8gd.2xlarge demonstrates average performance across general-purpose CPU tasks, multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, static web serving, and database operations. The server handles high-throughput operations effectively, such as Redis SET commands at 16.71 million operations per second and software compilation workloads. However, hardware limitations are evident in specific workloads; encryption test scores and small-model LLM text generation fall into weak performance categories, while prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models registers in the poor tier due to the lack of hardware accelerators and dedicated matrix extension flags.

The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with dedicated ARM physical cores offers high hardware resource density and favorable qualitative cost efficiency for input/output intensive compute tasks without the added expense of external block storage attachments. The instance is suited for high-concurrency web serving, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD code compilation, local scratch-space database processing, and batch data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture using AWS Graviton processors. It features 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, 16 GB of system RAM, and a bundled 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Driven by the Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place the instance in an average performance tier for general CPU processing, software compilation, static web serving, and memory bandwidth tests. However, performance drops on crypto-heavy tasks and large language model inference due to missing specialized instructions and discrete accelerators. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio combined with high-speed local storage yields a resource-dense configuration for temporary database processing, caching clusters, and automated build pipelines.
